deep.reconstruction: This folio carries no mathematics. It is page 7 of an Italian newspaper printed in Turin, 'Il Conte Cavour' (tipografia del giornale Il Conte Cavour, via Alfieri n. 3; F. Govean Direttore, V. Marenda Gerente). It contains foreign news: Mexico and Emperor Maximilian; cholera in Alexandria; the Queen of Holland; the abolition of the dazio in the Netherlands; earthquakes on Rhodes. It also contains telegraphic dispatches dated 3–5 July 1865 from Florence, Paris, New York (25 June), Vienna (Belcredi named minister of state) and the Paris Corps législatif and Senate (Dupin). Below these are the Paris Bourse closing prices of 3 July, the Turin Bourse prices of 5 July 1865, and an advertisement for P. Castiglioni, 'La riforma amministrativa e la questione degl'impiegati'. The only handwriting is archival: a pencilled word at the top, probably a cataloguer's label, and the folio number '149' in the right margin. There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct. The page matters to the historian only as physical evidence. Riemann was in Italy in 1865, and he evidently reused this newspaper sheet as scrap paper. The mathematical notes on the facing side are probably on the same physical sheet. They involve Π-products, bracket expansions of determinant-like symbols (z_1 y_1, …, z_{λ-1} y_{λ-1}), and the relations px = m(1-α)^2, etc. If they share the sheet, they would date from July 1865 or later, despite the bundle label 'MathNotizen1853'. That physical attribution is my inference and should be confirmed against the original sheet.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is printed newspaper text from July 1865 with no mathematical content. Its only interest is codicological: it suggests that notes in the '1853' bundle written on the same sheet date from Riemann's last Italian stay (1865–66).
transcription_corrections: The pencilled word at the top is not clearly 'Vorrei'. It is an archival or cataloguer's annotation (possibly 'Varia' or similar), not part of the printed text and not mathematical.
The Turin Bourse date reads '5 luglio 1865', which fixes the newspaper issue to early July 1865.
Turin Bourse line: the image reads '64 15. 74 20. 64 25. 64 10.' The '74 20' is likely a printer's error for 64 20; the transcription faithfully reproduces the print.

'149' is the archival folio number written in pencil in the right margin, not printed content.
